principles: Only fix the real learning-consumption gap; do not add broad automation for its own sake.
Preserve the evidence boundary: candidates are pending learning, active playbooks require explicit outcome proof.
Keep the command host-neutral and digest-bound using existing observeDigest/manifestDigest contracts.
Make DONE ingestion non-blocking and auditable through health/status rows.
Prefer reusing existing seed/proposal/candidate primitives over inventing a parallel pipeline.
drivers: Live store has settlement/proposable seeds but zero candidates or active playbooks.
Existing B-c28f/B-6703 primitives already enforce candidate inertness and evidence activation.
DONE gate safety requires learning failures not to block delivery or become gate evidence.

options.name: wrap-existing-primitives-and-hook-DONE
pros: Smallest correctness fix because it reuses observe/propose/approve digest checks
Keeps candidate and active boundaries consistent with B-c28f and B-6703
Easy to test with the existing playbook-seed-promotion-loop smoke
cons: Does not solve historical bulk backfill in the same story
Requires careful idempotency and health reporting around the wrapper

options.name: direct-active-on-DONE
pros: Would make active playbooks appear fastest
cons: Conflates story completion with verified learning usefulness
Violates evidence activation boundary and risks bad runtime guidance

options.name: timer-daemon-backfill
pros: Could eventually process many old seeds without manual intervention
cons: Too broad for the immediate correctness gap
Adds scheduling and historical batching risk before per-story ingestion is proven

rationale: This option fixes the real missing link from DONE/story seeds to candidate playbooks while preserving Proofbound evidence boundaries and reusing existing digest-bound primitives. It gives users visible candidate creation now without pretending candidates are proven active guidance.

preMortem.scenario: Ingestion creates duplicate candidates for the same DONE story.
preMortem.trigger: Repeated DONE hook or repeated playbook_candidate_ingest runs over the same canonical source.
preMortem.consequence: Runtime memory would see multiple candidate records for one source and promotion evidence could be double-counted.
preMortem.mitigation: Use existing represented-source checks, add story/source scoped idempotency assertions, and verify repeated ingest produces zero new candidates.

preMortem.trigger: Learning-store write, digest drift, or malformed seed error throws from post-DONE ingestion.
preMortem.consequence: A non-authoritative learning layer would break delivery, violating the gate boundary.
preMortem.mitigation: Run ingestion as best-effort non-blocking settlement follow-up and record failed/zero-created health diagnostics without failing DONE.

preMortem.scenario: Candidate ingestion accidentally activates playbooks or writes helped outcomes.
preMortem.trigger: Wrapper reuses promotion apply logic or records outcome rows while approving candidates.
preMortem.consequence: Story completion would become runtime guidance without exposure proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep wrapper limited to proposal/candidate writes, assert no playbook-auto-activations/outcomes are written, and keep playbook_auto_promotion_apply as the only activation path.
